note: Written by Claude from reputable outlets (Reuters and AP via syndication partners, ABC News, Al Jazeera, AFP, Kyodo, Yahoo Finance, Malay Mail, Korea JoongAng Daily, ANI and others); source under each story. US midterm results were not yet in at press time. Japan and India are shorter because fewer reputable reports could be retrieved this morning. Sports excluded.

items.headline: AMD's data-centre sales nearly double; strong Q4 outlook lifts shares
items.summary: AMD reported record third-quarter revenue of $13.4 billion, up 45%, with data-centre revenue up 97% to $8.5 billion. It guided to about $17 billion in fourth-quarter revenue, and the stock rose about 7% after hours.

items.headline: Chip stocks rebound after bear-market slide
items.summary: The Philadelphia semiconductor index jumped about 2.6% on Tuesday, a day after closing roughly 22% below its October peak. Memory and chip-equipment makers led the bounce.

items.headline: Apple slides on margin warning tied to memory shortage
items.summary: Apple shares fell about 4% after it forecast gross margins of 45–46%, blaming a global memory-chip shortage, and Greater China revenue missed expectations. Because the Dow is price-weighted, Apple's drop dragged that index lower.

items.headline: Shopify posts first revenue miss since 2022; stock tumbles
items.summary: Shopify's third-quarter revenue of $3.74 billion came in just short of forecasts, and merchandise volume of $119.2 billion also missed. The shares fell around 15–16%; Gartner and Dynatrace also slumped on growth and margin worries.

items.headline: CrowdStrike buys two AI-security start-ups for $495m
items.summary: CrowdStrike agreed to acquire Fiddler AI and Dreadnode for a combined $495 million, according to the Wall Street Journal, and its shares rose more than 2%.

items.headline: Nasdaq gains, Dow slips as Election Day trading ends
items.summary: The Nasdaq rose 0.8% to 25,372 and the S&P 500 added 0.4% to 7,569, while the Dow fell 0.4% to 51,787 on Apple's slide. Investors were braced for midterm results after the close.

items.headline: Oil swings as US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island cloud diplomacy
items.summary: Brent climbed above $106 early Tuesday after reported US strikes near the Strait of Hormuz, before easing as hopes for US–Iran talks persisted. Crude remains near four-week lows after Monday's roughly 7% drop.

items.headline: US job openings jump; long-dated Treasury yields climb
items.summary: September job openings rose to 7.5 million, above the 7.1 million expected, while layoffs fell. The 10-year Treasury yield rose to about 4.95%, and a Fed survey showed business credit demand contracting for the first time in over a year.

items.headline: Gold and silver slide; gold stays under $4,000
items.summary: Gold futures fell about 1.5% to around $3,912 an ounce and silver dropped nearly 4% to $48.90. Reuters noted gold has been moving with stocks rather than acting as a safe haven.

items.headline: Binance customers pull $4.6bn after record hack
items.summary: Withdrawals reached about $4.64 billion once Binance lifted its suspension, with net outflows near $3.64 billion. Investors also pulled more than $1 billion from US bitcoin funds in two days.

items.headline: MOM probes 45 firms over work-pass breaches at Changi Airport
items.summary: About 270 workers employed by contractors of ground handler SATS may have been deployed illegally, including Employment Pass holders found doing baggage handling. MOM has told SATS to tighten oversight of its contractors.

items.headline: Haze dominates Parliament with over 50 questions
items.summary: MPs pressed the government on holding companies accountable for Indonesian forest fires, after Singapore issued its first notices under the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act. Officials have signalled the law may be amended.

items.headline: MPs question plan to merge COE Categories A and B
items.summary: The LTA proposes a single car category, with surcharges and rebates tied to a vehicle's open market value. MPs asked how families and SMEs would be affected and how buyers would be protected from dealers absorbing rebates.

items.headline: Answers sought on nine-hour public healthcare IT outage
items.summary: MPs asked why backups failed during the October 13 network problem that hit all three public healthcare clusters and disrupted about 4,000 appointments. Synapxe has said there was no sign of a cyber attack.

items.headline: MAS offers S$30m grant to steer insurers into infrastructure
items.summary: MAS launched a S$30 million grant to help insurers build infrastructure-investment teams and proposed lower capital charges for qualifying infrastructure debt and senior securitisation tranches. Consultation closes on 18 December.

items.headline: Anwar warns Malaysia is exposed to sophisticated cyber attacks
items.summary: Malaysia's prime minister told Parliament the country's growth as a data-centre hub may make it a target, citing recent breaches abroad. Bank Negara is holding a special session with financial institutions.

items.headline: China tells Manila to rein in politicians crossing 'red lines'
items.summary: Foreign Minister Wang Yi told his Philippine counterpart that ties were being harmed by "malicious interference" and urged Manila to restrain critics of Beijing. Tensions have grown after a row over China's envoy last month.

items.headline: Indonesia bans routing resource exports through third countries
items.summary: Jakarta now requires natural-resource exports to ship directly to destination markets. It is also adding China and India as gasoline suppliers to shore up energy security.

items.headline: Laos plans to sell 500MW of renewable power to Singapore
items.summary: The deal would expand Laos's regional electricity exports and support development of the ASEAN Power Grid.

items.headline: Thailand tightens Myanmar border after spillover fighting
items.summary: Thai authorities stepped up security after clashes between Myanmar's military and rebels damaged homes and injured people on the Thai side. Separately, Thailand has logged 25.46 million foreign arrivals so far this year.
items.source: Bangkok Post and The Nation via Bernama

items.headline: Pacifist constitution turns 80 amid Takaichi's push to revise it
items.summary: Protesters rallied outside the Diet to defend the never-amended constitution on the anniversary of its promulgation. Prime Minister Takaichi wants to begin the amendment process, but cross-party consensus is lacking.

items.headline: Defence chief renews call to debate non-nuclear principles
items.summary: Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi again urged a review of Japan's three non-nuclear principles and backed considering nuclear-powered submarines. The government may reword the principles in security documents due by year-end.

items.headline: Kospi plunges 3.6% as AI-spending doubts hit chipmakers
items.summary: The index closed at 5,648.79 as foreigners sold a net 1.5 trillion won. SK hynix fell 5% and Samsung Electronics 4.2%, while refiners slid on lower oil prices.

items.headline: Lee calls for powerful new cybersecurity body
items.summary: President Lee Jae Myung said the current system of inspections and after-the-fact responses is showing clear limits. The spy agency has begun emergency security checks at more than 2,100 public bodies.

items.headline: North Korea rejects blame for $6.3bn Binance heist
items.summary: Kim Yo Jong called the FBI's accusation "absurd rhetoric" in a state-media statement. The FBI has attributed the theft to the TraderTraitor hacking unit.

items.headline: Seoul and Ankara sign nuclear financing pact during Erdogan visit
items.summary: Korea's Exim Bank and Turkey's state nuclear company agreed to explore funding for Turkish energy projects as Seoul bids for the planned Sinop plant. The leaders also agreed to expand joint defence production.

items.headline: RBA lifts cash rate to 4.85%, highest since 2008
items.summary: The Reserve Bank raised rates for a fifth time this year in a 6–3 vote, saying inflation will not fall below 3% until late 2027. Governor Michele Bullock left the door open to further rises.

items.headline: House prices fall for seventh month in a row
items.summary: Cotality data shows prices are falling at the fastest pace in 40 years. Liberal senator Andrew Bragg blamed the government's capital gains tax and negative gearing changes.

items.headline: Albanese meets King Charles and UK PM Burnham at CHOGM
items.summary: At the Commonwealth summit in Antigua, Albanese urged action to protect elected representatives and pitched Australia's bid for a UN Security Council seat. His talks with Andy Burnham covered AI, AUKUS and regional security.

items.headline: Gallagher insists $38bn in NDIS savings must be delivered
items.summary: The finance minister stood by the savings target after a reviewing actuary questioned whether it is achievable. The government is weighing savings measures ahead of the mid-year budget update.

items.headline: South Australia joins defence of under-16 social media ban
items.summary: SA will back the Commonwealth in the High Court challenge brought by Libertarian MP John Ruddick and the Digital Freedom Project.

items.headline: Polls close in midterms seen as a referendum on Trump
items.summary: Voting went relatively smoothly after a surge in early ballots, as Trump repeated unfounded fraud claims. Democrats need a net gain of a few Senate seats; prediction markets favoured them to win both chambers. Results were still to come at press time.
items.source: AP via PBS NewsHour; Yahoo Finance

items.headline: US carries out 'defensive' strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island
items.summary: US officials said the limited strikes targeted Iranian missile sites after an attack on a US aircraft in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran said the "ball is in the US court", while Trump said a deal could happen and ruled out strikes after the election.

items.headline: Trump says $4bn in annual aid to Israel will end
items.summary: Trump told Fox News the US will stop the yearly aid from 2027 but keep selling Israel arms, adding that Netanyahu had raised the idea. Netanyahu's office did not immediately comment.

items.headline: Trump says trade deal with Canada is close
items.summary: Trump said a deal would include tariff-free fertiliser supplies, and Prime Minister Carney said negotiating teams would work on it in the coming weeks.

items.headline: Election Day petrol prices hit record high
items.summary: The national average reached $4.14 a gallon for petrol and $6.29 for diesel, the highest ever on an Election Day, according to GasBuddy.

items.headline: PBOC raises FX reserve ratio to slow the yuan's rally
items.summary: The central bank lifted banks' foreign-currency reserve requirement from 4% to 6% from November 15, draining about $24 billion. The yuan posted its steepest daily drop in about six months, ending a 13-day winning streak.

items.headline: China's top general meets Russian defence minister
items.summary: Central Military Commission vice-chair Zhang Shengmin told Andrei Belousov that Beijing wants deeper military cooperation with Moscow. It was Zhang's first known meeting with a foreign minister since joining the Politburo.

items.headline: Wang Yi accuses Manila of 'malicious interference'
items.summary: In a call with Philippine Foreign Secretary Theresa Lazaro, China's foreign minister urged Manila to restrain politicians who attack Beijing, amid a series of diplomatic spats.

items.headline: Trade surplus on track to top $1 trillion again
items.summary: Reuters noted the yuan is up more than 10% against the dollar since the April 2025 tariffs, while China's trade surplus is heading above $1 trillion for a second year.

items.headline: Sensex and Nifty rise for a fourth straight session
items.summary: The Sensex gained 1.6% to 76,918 and the Nifty 1.6% to 23,811, led by consumer-goods stocks, even as crude edged higher after the Qeshm strikes.

items.headline: 23 Indians killed so far in West Asia conflict, MEA says
items.summary: The dead include 15 seafarers, five of them killed in attacks on shipping in the Black Sea; one sailor died when an Indian vessel was attacked off Oman. India urged de-escalation and freedom of navigation.

items.headline: Air India to move more Europe and US flights to Mumbai
items.summary: CEO Tewolde Gebremariam said Pakistan's airspace closure is hurting Delhi operations, and the airline is exploring Bengaluru as a third hub.
